Area.evidence_source: A common factor involved in both male and female suicides was alcohol consumption and its sequelae, including financial loss, increased stress, shame, violence, and disability. Nearly half of the deceased men were reported to have alcohol problems that greatly contributed to their suicide. ... Alcohol was commonly blamed for negative family relationships, poverty, and abusive behavior: ... Not only was alcohol endorsed as a precursor to suicidal behavior of the one drinking, but it was also blamed for causing the suicide of another family member. ... perpetuating poverty, and sustaining a sense of hopelessness for the whole family. ... Several young men (five under 30 years) were described as addicted to alcohol, perpetuating their emotional despair.
